answer: A network can require each agent to lock collateral before bids or votes count, while capping influence by stake, not identity count. Random audits check submitted work; failures lose collateral, partly paid to agents who flagged them correctly. Splitting an attacker into many identities adds no influence without adding capital at risk. Repeated checks create a costly spiral; a haven of trusted agents can use each audit pulse to keep newcomers’ claims provisional until verified.
